::: {.callout-tip}
## Why This Matters
An Indian EMS company that successfully pivoted into semiconductor OSAT — proof that domestic firms can compete in chipmaking.
:::

## What does this facility make?

Assembles and tests semiconductor chips for various applications. Kaynes started as an electronics manufacturing services (EMS) company and expanded upstream into chip packaging.

## Why does it matter?

Most ISM projects involve foreign technology partners. Kaynes is notable as a homegrown Indian company that built OSAT capability — showing that the Indian private sector can move up the semiconductor value chain, not just multinational corporations.

## Project Timeline

- **01 Sep 2024** — Approved under ISM
- **01 Dec 2024** — Construction begins at Sanand
- **31 Mar 2026** — PM Modi inaugurates Kaynes semiconductor plant — facility goes operational
- **19 Sep 2026** — IndieSemiC (fabless design startup) and Kaynes Semicon sign an MoU for OSAT collaboration — qualification, assembly, and testing of QFN/BGA and other packages for IndieSemiC's low-power SiP modules and discrete devices, plus joint work on design-for-manufacturability and new package introduction
- **24 Sep 2026** — Company guidance (CEO Raghu Panicker): Unit 2 at Sanand targeted to become operational in December 2026, including a ~$50 million automotive-grade reliability and failure-analysis lab — one of the first of its kind in Asia, starting with automotive qualification before expanding to space-grade semiconductors. Forward guidance, not yet confirmed by an inauguration.



## Supply Chain

Equipment, gas, and materials suppliers with their own tracked India facility feeding this project:

- **[Linde India — Sanand Specialty Gas Facility](../equipment-firms/linde-sanand-gas-facility.html)** — High-purity specialty gases for chip packaging/assembly-and-test operations.
